Item 1. Business

Acme builds industrial robots for factories and warehouses. Its engineers design motion-control systems, safety equipment, and software used by manufacturers around the world.

Customers use Acme products to automate repetitive work, improve product quality, and operate production lines more efficiently across many industries and regions.

Acme sells products through a direct sales force and qualified distribution partners. The company also provides installation, maintenance, training, and technical support services.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Acme's operations and financial results could be harmed by interruptions in the supply of electronic components, motors, sensors, and other materials used in its products.

Demand for industrial automation can change with customer capital spending, economic conditions, manufacturing activity, and the availability of financing in key markets.

Competition from established automation vendors and new entrants could reduce prices, delay customer orders, increase development costs, or weaken Acme's market position.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis

Revenue increased as customers expanded automation projects in automotive, logistics, and electronics markets. Service revenue also grew with the installed base of equipment.

Gross margin reflected product mix, component costs, manufacturing utilization, and investments in new technology. Management continues to monitor supply and demand trends.

Acme expects research and development spending to support new products, software capabilities, and safety features while maintaining disciplined operating expense management.
